claim.markdown_says: 04FA-052F, 1C80-1C88, 1D2B, 1D78, 2DE0-2DFF, A640-A66F, A674-A67D, A67F-A69F, FE2E-FE2F Deseret:   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 49087) ... then page-1215 opens with the bare line '10400-1044F' with no label
claim.why_it_matters: Both the Cyrillic continuation range 'FE2E-FE2F' and the following script label 'Deseret:' were pulled back from PDF page 1185 onto the last line of page 1184. The 'Deseret:' label is glued to a Cyrillic range list, and Deseret's own range '10400-1044F' opens the next page unlabelled. Content belonging to page 1215 is attributed to page 1214, so a citation by page anchor lands on the wrong page.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against both rendered pages. RENDERED PDF p1214 (printed folio 1184, verified in a 2x upscaled crop of the bottom 12% of the page): the final text block is exactly 'Cyrillic:' / '0483-0484, 0487, 048A-048B, 04C5-04C6, 04C9-04CA, 04CD-04CF, 04F6-04F7,' / '04FA-052F, 1C80-1C88, 1D2B, 1D78, 2DE0-2DFF, A640-A66F, A674-A67D, A67F-A69F,' followed by white space and the footer '1184 (c)ISO/IEC 2023'. Neither 'FE2E-FE2F' nor 'Deseret:' appears anywhere on PDF p1214 -- the claim's quotation of the PDF is accurate. RENDERED PDF p1215 (printed folio 1185, top-16% crop): the first body line is 'FE2E-FE2F', then a blank line, then 'Deseret:' as its own standalone label line, then '10400-1044F'. MARKDOWN, specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 49087, quoted verbatim: '04FA-052F, 1C80-1C88, 1D2B, 1D78, 2DE0-2DFF, A640-A66F, A674-A67D, A67F-A69F, FE2E-FE2F Deseret:' -- the claim's quotation of the markdown is exact, including the line number. Line 49088 is blank and line 49089 is the '<a id="page-1215">' anchor, so 'Deseret:' definitively sits inside the page-1214 slice; line 49093, the first body line of page 1215, is the bare '10400-1044F' with no preceding label. So this is NOT a case of the text being present-but-reflowed, NOT a misquote, and NOT ordinary hyphenation. It survives the adversarial tests because the label-to-range association -- the sole semantic content of this Unicode script-range table -- is destroyed: a consumer of the markdown reads 'Deseret:' as a trailing token of the Cyrillic enumeration, and reads '10400-1044F' as an orphan with no owning script. That the same table elsewhere in the document (lines 40287/40297) handles an identical Deseret page break correctly, keeping 'Deseret:' on its own line, confirms the p1214 form is a transcription defect rather than a house convention. Confidence is high; no text is lost, but it is mis-associated and mis-paginated.
verdict.corrected_description: REAL, but the claim overstates one of its two halves and understates the other. (1) The 'FE2E-FE2F' half is essentially benign reflow: it is the tail of a comma-continued range list that wraps across the page break, and the markdown joins it correctly as '... A67F-A69F, FE2E-FE2F' with the continuation comma preserved. The only cost is page attribution -- a citation anchored to page-1215 will not find that token, which now lives in the page-1214 slice. (2) The 'Deseret:' half is the actual structural defect and is worse than a pagination issue: the script label is concatenated onto the END of a data line, space-separated, with no line break and no blank line ('... A67F-A69F, FE2E-FE2F Deseret:'). This severs the label-to-range binding in a table whose entire meaning is that binding -- 'Deseret:' reads as part of the Cyrillic range enumeration, and Deseret's range '10400-1044F' opens page 1215 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 49093) as an unlabelled orphan. Correct transcription requires a paragraph break before 'Deseret:' and moving that label plus its range into the page-1215 slice, matching the layout the same document already uses for the identical Deseret page break at lines 40287/40297. Note the printed-folio vs PDF-page offset of 30: PDF page 1214 = printed 1184, PDF page 1215 = printed 1185.
